video_metadata.working_title: TEXAS 1974 Cold Case Solved After 46 Years — Justice for Carla Walker
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: In the early hours of February 17, 1974, 17-year-old Carla Walker was taken from her boyfriend's car in the Ridglea Bowl parking lot in Fort Worth after a Valentine's dance; the man questioned and cleared in March 1974, Glen Samuel McCurley, was identified 46 years later through forensic genetic genealogy, arrested on September 21, 2020, and pleaded guilty on August 24, 2021.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: grief turning into quiet vindication: the answer had been sitting in the 1974 file all along

protagonist._instructions: The main character of your story - can be hero, villain, or antihero. Fill with verified facts only.
protagonist.full_name: Glen Samuel McCurley (perpetrator; convicted by guilty plea). The heart of the story is the victim, Carla Jan Walker.
protagonist.age_at_time_of_events: Age 77 at his arrest on September 21, 2020 and 78 at his plea in August 2021 [9][11][26]; by arithmetic he was about 30 or 31 in February 1974 (computed, not stated in sources). Died at 80 in July 2023 [8].
protagonist.occupation_or_status: In 1974 an ex-convict (by his own statement to detectives, per the 2020 arrest affidavit) who owned a .22 caliber Ruger [7][9][10]. In 2020 he was living quietly in Fort Worth [5 Texas Monthly = source 7].
protagonist.physical_description: Not used. No verified physical description gathered.
protagonist.background_brief: In 1974 detectives traced a pistol magazine found at the abduction scene to a .22 Ruger; ATF purchase records gave about two dozen local buyers and McCurley was one of them. In early March 1974 two detectives visited his home; he said the Ruger had been stolen from his pickup about six weeks earlier while he was fishing, that he had not reported the theft because he was an ex-convict, and that his wife had been in West Texas at the time. He agreed to a polygraph, passed, and was cleared [7][9][15].
protagonist.psychological_profile: Not speculated. Documented behaviour only: denied knowing Carla in 1974 and again in September 2020 ('I've never seen her'), then broke down in the recorded interview and admitted choking her [24][25][26].
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: Not used for the perpetrator (style rule: never glamorise).

victims_or_targets._instructions: People affected by the protagonist's actions. Include 3-5 key figures minimum.

individuals.name: Carla Jan Walker [MINOR, 17]
individuals.role_or_profession: Junior at Western Hills High School (Fort Worth ISD, Benbrook area); cheerleader; tennis team member [5][15][16]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Stranger. Abducted from the passenger seat of her boyfriend's car in the Ridglea Bowl parking lot in the early hours of February 17, 1974; found in a culvert near Benbrook Lake on February 20, 1974 [1][9][15]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Kidnapped, sexually assaulted and strangled (plain legal fact only; no detail) [2][9]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Described by her sister Cindy as funny, sweet, tough and stubborn, a 'little spitfire'; at 16 she told her family she wanted a new Monte Carlo and her parents got it for her; popular with many girlfriends; her brother Jim thought she would go to college and become a veterinarian [16]

individuals.name: Rodney McCoy
individuals.role_or_profession: Carla's boyfriend in 1974; the only living witness other than the killer [14]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Struck in the head with a pistol by the attacker; never saw his face [14]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Knocked unconscious; the gun was pointed inches from his head and clicked three times without firing; later placed on the 2019 list of more than 80 possible suspects that the cold case detectives reviewed [14][15]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Drove to the Walker home with blood running into his eyes and banged on the door; testified at the 2021 trial [14]
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: 'I was in shock' (what he told the family, as reported from his 2021 testimony) [14]

individuals.name: Jim Walker
individuals.role_or_profession: Carla's younger brother; 12 years old in 1974 [11][13]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Spoke at the September 22, 2020 press conference and addressed McCurley in court in August 2021 [11][12][5]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Grew up in the shadow of the case; graduated from Western Hills High, attended Sam Houston State University, planned to become a detective to get his hands on Carla's files; for years called the Fort Worth police cold case unit asking about developments [7]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Wept at the 2020 press conference [13]; told the court he had managed to forgive his sister's killer [5]; later served on the board of the FWPD Cold Case Support Group [33]
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: 'The word that came across my brain was finally, finally.' / 'This is a resolution that's been prayed for.' [11]; 'Carla was tiny, but mighty.' [16]

individuals.name: Cindy (Walker) Stone
individuals.role_or_profession: Carla's older sister; closest sibling, 'not only sisters, but best friends' [16]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Delivered a victim impact statement on August 24, 2021 [2][5][36]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Said the unresolved case shattered family milestones and relationships; said McCurley put her family through hell [5]
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: 'I wish you'd done this a long time ago.' [5][36] (AP renders it 'I wish you had done this a long time ago.' [2]); 'I knew her.' and 'You had choices.' [5]

collective_victims_if_applicable.group_description: The Walker family (parents and siblings) and the unsolved-case families of Fort Worth
collective_victims_if_applicable.total_number_affected: Not quantified. A downtown Fort Worth rally raised awareness of about 1,000 unsolved cold cases (single source, date not verified) [news.yahoo rally item, not numbered; not used in script]
collective_victims_if_applicable.range_of_impacts: Decades without an answer; milestones overshadowed [5]

characters.name: Detective Leah Wagner, Fort Worth Police Department
characters.key_actions_they_took: Joined FWPD in 2000, patrol first, detective in 2013, moved to the cold case unit in 2018 when she was its sole staffer; returned Jim Walker's calls; reopened the case with Bennett in 2019; sent Carla's dress, bra and underwear for testing; received the September 4, 2020 lab call [7][9][11][15]

characters.name: Detective Jeff Bennett, Fort Worth Police Department (CBS renders the first name 'Jay')
characters.key_actions_they_took: Reopened the case in 2019; called Paul Holes about the tiny remaining DNA; visited Othram's lab; sent a piece of Carla's bra to Othram CEO David Mittelman; interviewed McCurley at home in September 2020; later created the FWPD Cold Case Support Group nonprofit [11][18][33]
characters.notable_quotes: 'We had a very, very small amount left, which is not typically usable.' and told Holes he had 'four nanograms of DNA' [18]

characters.name: Paul Holes
characters.role_in_story: Retired investigator; host of Oxygen's 'The DNA of Murder with Paul Holes'
characters.key_actions_they_took: Introduced Fort Worth detectives to Othram after the evidence produced no CODIS hit; Oxygen paid for the testing according to reporting [7][17][18]

characters.name: David Mittelman
characters.role_in_story: CEO of Othram Inc., The Woodlands, Texas
characters.key_actions_they_took: Received the bra sample; Othram built a profile and uploaded the data to GEDmatch [18][20]

characters.name: Judge Elizabeth Beach
characters.key_actions_they_took: Sentenced McCurley to life in prison on August 24, 2021 [2][5]

characters.name: Sharen Wilson
characters.key_actions_they_took: Office decided not to seek the death penalty (announced May 2021) [23]
characters.notable_quotes: Said Fort Worth police 'never gave up.' [2]

characters.name: Senators John Cornyn (R-Texas) and Peter Welch (D-Vermont)
characters.role_in_story: Sponsors of the Carla Walker Act
characters.key_actions_they_took: Introduced the bill December 12, 2024; reintroduced May 22, 2025; Senate passed it unanimously in June 2026 [27][28][29][30]
characters.notable_quotes: Cornyn: 'This bill creates a pilot program to fund the use of forensic genetic genealogy, which enables law enforcement to investigate and prosecute cold cases and other hard-to-solve crimes.' [28]

chronological_timeline._instructions: List every significant event with exact dates when possible. This is the backbone of your script.

events.location: Western Hills High School, Benbrook/Fort Worth
events.what_happened: Carla, 17, attends the school's Valentine's dance with boyfriend Rodney McCoy; Dateline reports the theme was 'Love is a Kaleidoscope'

events.location: Parking lot of Brunswick Ridglea Bowl, west Fort Worth
events.what_happened: Sitting in McCoy's car, the couple is approached by an armed man who strikes McCoy with a pistol, pulls Carla from the passenger seat and takes her; the gun clicked three times without firing; McCoy blacks out; police later said the man told McCoy 'I am going to kill you'
McCoy drives to the Walker house with blood running into his eyes, bangs on the door, tells the family what happened
A magazine from a .22 caliber Ruger is found at the scene
events.significance: The 1974 clue that pointed at McCurley

events.location: Culvert near Benbrook Lake, about 30 minutes south(-west) of Fort Worth
events.what_happened: Carla's body is found three days after the abduction; she had been sexually assaulted and strangled
events.significance: Discovery; clothing (dress, bra, underwear) preserved as evidence

events.what_happened: After tracing the magazine to a .22 Ruger and pulling ATF purchase records (about two dozen buyers), two detectives visit McCurley; he says his Ruger was stolen from his pickup about six weeks earlier while fishing, that he did not report it because he was an ex-convict, and that his wife was in West Texas; he passes a polygraph and is cleared
events.significance: The killer is questioned and released in the first weeks

events.what_happened: An anonymous handwritten letter is sent to a detective saying the writer might know who was responsible; it contains 'Sign 10100'
events.significance: A lead that went nowhere; resurfaced in 2019

events.what_happened: Leah Wagner joins FWPD in 2000, becomes a detective in 2013, joins the cold case unit in 2018 as its sole staffer
events.significance: The detective who answers Jim Walker's calls

events.what_happened: Jim Walker reaches out to Fort Worth police asking for a fresh look
Police publicly release the 1974 anonymous letter seeking its author

Detectives Leah Wagner and Jeff Bennett reopen the case; build a list of more than 80 possible suspects; send Carla's dress, bra and underwear for testing; a male DNA profile from the bra yields no CODIS hit

After an introduction by Paul Holes, Bennett and Wagner visit Othram and send a piece of Carla's bra to CEO David Mittelman; about four nanograms of DNA remain; Othram builds a profile and uploads it to GEDmatch; genealogy points to the McCurley family and narrows to three brothers

events.location: Curbside bin at McCurley's Fort Worth home
events.what_happened: Investigators collect three items from his trash and send them for DNA testing (one account mentions a drinking straw)
Wagner is told by the lab that DNA from the trash matches the profile from Carla's bra
Bennett and Wagner interview McCurley; he denies knowing or killing Carla and consents to two mouth swabs
McCurley's swab matches the DNA on Carla's bra
events.source: [9] (day inferred from 'last Wednesday' in Sept. 22 report)

events.what_happened: McCurley, 77, is arrested without incident and charged with capital murder; held in Tarrant County Jail, bond $100,000; recorded police interview in which he first says 'I've never seen her' and later admits choking her
Jim Walker, in tears, thanks police: 'finally, finally'; '46 years, 7 months and 5 days'
Grand jury indicts McCurley, 77, for capital murder
Prosecutors announce they will not seek the death penalty
events.significance: Life in prison is the goal

events.what_happened: Capital murder trial; Rodney McCoy testifies; jurors watch the 2020 interview video

On the third day of trial McCurley, 78, waives the jury and pleads guilty to capital murder; Judge Elizabeth Beach sentences him to life in prison; families embrace; Cindy Stone and Jim Walker address him
Skip Hollandsworth reports police suspected Carla was not his only victim

events.location: Telford Unit (state prison), Bowie County, Texas
events.what_happened: McCurley dies of natural causes at 80, less than three years after his arrest; he had been a person of interest in three other murders but was never charged with them
Senators Cornyn and Welch introduce the Carla Walker Act
Bill reintroduced in the new Congress

Senate passes the Carla Walker Act unanimously; creates a pilot program to fund forensic genetic genealogy; House companion led by Reps. Wesley Hunt and Mike Simpson; no House vote found as of October 2026

cold_open_material._instructions: The most dramatic moment of your story - this will be your hook.

the_moment.exact_location: Brunswick Ridglea Bowl parking lot, west Fort Worth, Texas
the_moment.what_is_happening: Two teenagers in a parked car after a Valentine's dance; an armed man approaches the passenger side
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: A 17-year-old taken from a car with her boyfriend beside her; the gun clicked three times
the_moment.ironic_twist: Within weeks, detectives sat in the killer's home, heard his story about a stolen gun, watched him pass a polygraph, and cleared him. His name stayed in the file for 46 years.

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: How could the man who left a gun magazine in the parking lot be questioned in 1974 and stay free until 2020?

the_method._instructions: How did the protagonist do what they did? Technical details that can be explained to a general audience.
the_method.technique_name: Forensic genetic genealogy (FGG) with forensic-grade genome sequencing (Othram) and GEDmatch
step_by_step_explanation: Detectives sent Carla's preserved clothing (dress, bra, underwear) for modern testing [15]
A single-source male DNA profile was developed from material on the bra; it produced no hit in CODIS, the FBI's national database of known offenders and arrestees [15][19]
Only about four nanograms of DNA remained, an amount Bennett said is 'not typically usable' [18]

Othram, a lab in The Woodlands near Houston, used forensic-grade genome sequencing to read tens to hundreds of thousands of genetic markers (SNPs), far more than the roughly 20 markers used by CODIS (CODIS figure: background knowledge) [18][20][37]
The data were uploaded to GEDmatch, a public genealogy comparison site where users opt in; matches were distant relatives of the unknown man [18]
Building family trees from those relatives pointed to the McCurley family and three brothers [9][15]
Glen McCurley's name was already in the 1974 file because of the Ruger magazine [7][15]
On July 7, 2020 detectives collected three items from his curbside trash; on September 4 the lab reported a match [9]
A consensual two-swab sample confirmed the match on September 16, 2020 [9][10]
the_method.why_it_worked: The clothing had been preserved since 1974, and sequencing could extract enough markers from a tiny, degraded sample to search for relatives instead of the killer himself.

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: The FBI's national DNA database; it can only find a person whose own profile is already in it
A single letter of the genetic code that varies between people; genealogy compares hundreds of thousands of them
A genealogy website where people upload their own DNA files to find relatives; police can compare against users who allow it
A billionth of a gram; four nanograms is invisible to the eye
Items a person throws away at the curb can be collected and tested without a warrant in this kind of investigation

the_method.scale_of_operation: More than 80 possible suspects on the 2019 list [15]; about two dozen Ruger buyers in 1974 [7]; three brothers after genealogy [9]

systemic_failure._instructions: What institution, system, or authority failed to prevent this?
systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: The 1974 investigation (Fort Worth police task force)
systemic_failure.how_they_were_supposed_to_protect: Follow the physical clue, the .22 Ruger magazine, to its owner
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: They found the owner but accepted his unreported 'stolen gun' story and a passed polygraph; the task force cleared him and, per Texas Monthly, a lead detective later acknowledged they never thought about him again [7]
specific_incompetence_examples: An ex-convict who said his gun was stolen six weeks earlier had never reported the theft [9][10]
Reliance on a polygraph result to clear a suspect [7][15]
An anonymous 1974 letter sat in the file until it was released in 2019 [21][22]
By 2018 the cold case unit had a single staffer [7]
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The name that DNA delivered in 2020 had been in the case file since March 1974.

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Fort Worth Police Department Cold Case Unit, with Othram Inc.; Tarrant County Criminal District Attorney's Office prosecuted
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: That the Ruger owner's stolen-gun story and polygraph cleared him
the_investigation.key_breakthrough: Genome sequencing of about four nanograms of DNA from Carla's bra, uploaded to GEDmatch, leading to the McCurley family
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: The 1974 magazine linked to his gun; in 2020, his discarded trash
the_investigation.how_long_until_caught: 46 years, 7 months and 4 days (February 17, 1974 to September 21, 2020; computed)

the_confrontation._instructions: The arrest, raid, or climactic moment when everything collapses.
the_confrontation.protagonist_reaction: In the recorded interview he first said 'I've never seen her', then broke down in tears and admitted choking her [24][25]
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: Days before, he had denied everything at his own door and agreed to give the swabs that confirmed the match [9]

legal_resolution.trial_date_if_applicable: Late August 2021; plea on the third day, August 24, 2021 [2][5]
legal_resolution.notable_court_testimony: Rodney McCoy described the gun clicking three times and blacking out [14]; jurors watched the 2020 interview: 'I choked her to death, I guess' / 'I'm guilty' [2][25]

victim_impact_statements.key_quote: I wish you'd done this a long time ago.
victim_impact_statements.emotional_impact: Said he put the family through hell; urged him to confess any other crimes [2][5][36]

victim_impact_statements.key_quote: No verbatim quote verified; reported that he told McCurley he had managed to forgive him [5]

legal_resolution.sentence_received: Life in prison (AP: 'life in prison'; Star-Telegram/Wikipedia: life without parole; parole wording disputed, see notes) [2][8][1]
legal_resolution.protagonist_statement_in_court: Pleaded guilty; no verified allocution text
legal_resolution.current_status: Glen Samuel McCurley died of natural causes in July 2023, aged 80, in the Telford state prison in Bowie County, while serving his life sentence. He was convicted only of Carla Walker's murder. He was a person of interest in three other killings but was never charged with them [8]. The Carla Walker Act passed the U.S. Senate unanimously in June 2026; no House vote found as of October 2026 [27][28][29].

[37] General background context (well-established public facts, not re-verified this session because the search budget was exhausted): CODIS, the FBI's national DNA index (national level operational in 1998; about 20 core STR markers since 2017); DNA fingerprinting discovered by Alec Jeffreys in 1984; GEDmatch founded 2010; Golden State Killer (Joseph James DeAngelo) arrested April 24, 2018 after genetic genealogy using GEDmatch; Othram founded in 2018; February 1974 context: Watergate investigation (Nixon resigned August 9, 1974), the 1973-74 Arab oil embargo and gasoline lines, Patty Hearst kidnapped in Berkeley on February 4, 1974. AMBER Alert origin: 9-year-old Amber Hagerman abducted in Arlington, Texas, on January 13, 1996; the alert system created in the Dallas-Fort Worth area in 1996. Fort Worth slogan 'Where the West Begins'; Dallas about 30 miles east of Fort Worth; Valentine's Day 1974 fell on a Thursday (calendar).

next_video_hook.teaser_line: In 1993 a woman was killed in her Minneapolis apartment. Twenty-six years later, the answer came from a napkin a man threw away at his son's hockey game.
